gen-luckiest-guy-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads sturdy and welcoming, with a hefty lowercase and broad counters that stay open on every curve. Luckiest Guy brings loud, poured-ink letters in one width, and the sans-serif body simply keeps its footing.
gen-tourney-switzer: Switzer reads light and approachable, with wire-like letterforms, a tall waist line and c tips that keep their distance. Tourney is the loud one, wide-tracked and chunky, cut at a single width.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-be-vietnam-p: Playful pixel-era swagger, stretched out with generous tracking and a high x-height line, then Be Vietnam Pro behind it. Its bent-rod strokes never shift from heavy to light, and that clean consistency is the real strength.
gen-megrim-fs-public-sans: Thin steel-rod angles, bent into futuristic letters with open, paperclip-like curves. Megrim sets the sci-fi tone up top, and Public Sans grounds it with a hefty, low-slung sans that never competes.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-cascadia-code: Wallpoet cuts its tall letters like stencil work, with paper showing through the gaps. Cascadia Code runs on a wire-thin monoline skeleton and spaced-out letters, so longer text moves at a deliberate, even tempo.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-cascadia-mono: Stencil-cut towers, loud and commanding. Wallpoet carries all the drama, while Cascadia Mono stays compact and tidy, its curves matching its stems in thickness like pins standing in a board.
gen-righteous-manrope: Fat, round and full of fun, with bowls that fill the line. Righteous takes the spotlight with its bent-rod energy, but Manrope holds its own with bright open curves and a pen line that never wavers.
gen-audiowide-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads like it was drawn with a single nib, its bodies nearly as tall as the capitals. Audiowide, with tile-like glyphs and wide grout gaps, makes the pairing feel like a long, easy scroll through a plain sans.
gen-eater-gf-lexend-giga: Eater has a spooky, aggressive bite, yet its mild stroke contrast stays oddly friendly, with wide gaps between letters. Lexend Giga counters with flat glass-tube lines, and the clash is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-flavors-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, with open curves and letters spaced like stepping stones. Flavors, whimsical and towering, makes that sans-serif calm feel like a deliberate, well-judged foil.
